messages:
aleks: Heads up — noticed a steady bump in streaming token volume from our EU customers over the last 3 weeks. Context lengths up ~2.8x on some routes. Need a quick sanity-check on GPU hour forecasts for Q2 and whether we should pre-warm eu-west pools. :thinking:

sana: Can you share the per-route breakdown? is this concentrated on chat-stream or batch-completion?

aleks: Mostly chat-stream (live summarization + multi-turn). Non-stream traffic is flat. Quick paste of rolling 7d: tokens_per_min by route:
```
/chat-stream: 1.9B tpm (+180%)
/video-summ: 0.6B tpm (+320%)
/qa-batch: 0.45B tpm (+4%)
```

jordan: whoa video-summ spike is huge. Are these long prefix contexts or more frequent short messages?

aleks: Long prefixes. Median context length for video-summ jumped from ~1.1k to ~3.2k. Streaming keeps the 99th p95 latency reasonable but increases token churn and KV cache churn.

mike: ops note — eu-west has 2x less available p4d slots this month due to partner maintenance window. If we don't reserve, burst may fail and fall back to slower quantized variants (higher latency).

autoscale-bot: [alert] autoscaler notified: eu-west streaming pool reached 78% reserved capacity at 2026-03-17T09:12Z. Suggested actions: scale up +1 node or shift low-priority traffic to dedicated batch pool.

ops_lead: @sana @jordan can you run a cost vs latency simulation for pre-warming an extra 4 GPUs for 6 weeks vs letting fallback kick in for peak 3 hours/day? Need $ delta and expected 95th latency impact.

sana: I'll run a quick back-of-envelope now. Assumptions: p4d spot-style commit = $15/hr, pre-warm 4 GPUs for 6 weeks => 4 * 24 * 7 * 6 * $15 = $120,960 (rough). Fallback to quantized v2 increases p95 by ~120ms and reduces cost per token by ~30%.

jordan: If we pre-warm, we reduce KV cache misses and can use non-quantized kernels for video-summ which preserves quality. Also avoids cross-region routing which adds ~30ms.

aleks: My ask: give me a per-week GPU-hour addition and a schedule recommendation. We expect peak windows UTC 07:00-10:00 and 16:00-19:00 (EU customer activity).

sana: Quick projection (weekly):
```
baseline: 420 gpu-hrs/wk
streaming surge: +160 gpu-hrs/wk
buffer (safety/region failover): +40 gpu-hrs/wk
=> recommended reserve: 620 gpu-hrs/wk (~48% increase)
```

mike: Note network egress on those nodes will also spike ~2.2x. Ops will need to bump bandwidth caps for the eu-west subnet or we'll hit throttling.

ops_lead: Can we reduce token churn instead of capacity? Ideas: earlier prefix trimming, KV prefetch heuristics, or configurable max_context for video-summ. Any quick wins?

aleks: We rolled a small experiment with aggressive prefix trimming on 10% of video-summ traffic last week. Token volume dropped 27% and user QA metrics stayed within tolerance. Might be a good short-term knob.

jordan: Proposed plan: week 1: apply prefix-trim to 30% of video-summ traffic + request 4 additional GPUs for 2 weeks to cover immediate burst. Monitor error/quality. Week 2-4: if traffic persists, extend reserve to full 6 weeks and consider dedicated reserved capacity product for that customer segment.

mike: I'll open the infra ticket to request capacity and network bump. tagging infra-ops and billing for approval.

autoscale-bot: [info] ticket infra-5428 created by mike: request eu-west +4 GPUs and bandwidth increase.

aleks: sweet — thanks. Let's re-run forecast after 7 days and decide on the 6-week commit. Also add a metric for KV-cache miss rate to the weekly dashboard. :thumbsup:
